claims.text: HEA resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion is governed by formation of a stable, self-healing passivating surface film.
The protective surface film is enriched in noble elements.
A refined, high-entropy microstructure supports the passivating film.
The passivating film minimizes local chemical gradients.
A uniform nanocrystalline grain structure inhibits crack initiation and propagation during mechanical stress.
Fine nanocrystalline grains and beneficial dual-phase interfaces promote preferential enrichment of noble elements at the surface.
Preferential surface enrichment produces a continuous, adherent oxide or passivation layer.
High configurational entropy and sluggish diffusion promote uniform elemental distribution and nanostructuring under combined mechanical and corrosive stress.
Uniform elemental distribution and nanostructuring facilitate formation of a protective, self-healing passivation film.
The passivation film minimizes localized anodic sites.
The passivation film resists removal during mechanical wear.
The proposed film decreases chemical dissolution.
The proposed film decreases abrasive material loss.
Under simultaneous wear-corrosion testing, the refined HEA will have lower wear volume than a conventional or coarse-grained baseline.
Under simultaneous wear-corrosion testing, the refined HEA will have a lower corrosion rate than the baseline.
Synergistic protection will be strongest when attack permits passivation but wear does not completely remove the film.
The prediction may fail under ultra-high wear, extremely aggressive corrosion, or temperatures that disrupt the film or substantially alter the grain structure.
A statistically significant failure to improve both wear and corrosion metrics relative to the baseline is designated as falsifying the hypothesis.
